descriptionChirho: First-person singular reflexive pronoun used in genitive ('of myself'), dative ('to/for myself'), and accusative ('myself') cases to indicate the speaker as both subject and object of the action. All inflectional forms express the same reflexive self-reference. Multilingual evidence: eng 'myself/of myself/to myself', spa 'mi mismo/de mi mismo/para mi mismo', hin 'apne aap/apne liye/apna' (oneself/for oneself/one's own), arb 'nafsi/li-nafsi' (my soul/for my soul), kor 'na jasin/na jasin-ege' (my self/to my self), swa 'mwenyewe/kwangu/yangu' (himself/at mine/mine). Paul uses it extensively to describe his own apostolic conduct (1 Cor 4:6, 2 Cor 11:7, Phil 3:13).
